notes:
Summary: Meridian is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for mission-critical inference in trading and fraud pipelines. Primary ask is a deterministic throughput guarantee for steady-state trading workloads plus a defined burst policy for market open/close spikes. They are risk-averse on availability and want firm minima rather than probabilistic estimates.

Highlights / fragments from calls: 
- 'We need 120k tokens/sec sustained across 80 concurrent sessions during market hours.' (Head of ML)
- 'Burst must be usable without manual ops intervention; prefer token credits or automated short-term scale.' (Infrastructure lead)
- Security: must run in their VPC with HSM-backed KMS, SOC2 evidence, and audit logs forwarded to Splunk.
- They want explicit GPU equivalence in the SOW (e.g., 12x A100-40GB equivalent reserved) and clear failover to private pool when Dedicated capacity is saturated.

Important: Procurement pushed back on open-ended burst pricing — they want a capped burst allowance per month and defined throttling behavior when exceeded. Legal redlines on SLA measurement window (5-minute vs 1-minute) are still unresolved.

requirements_summary: Workload types: low-latency chat for traders, synchronous anti-fraud reranking on transaction write path, embeddings for personalization
Latency targets: p95 <= 120ms for chat gen (short prompts), p99 <= 300ms for reranking (100 item list)
Availability: 99.95% SLA during market hours (09:00-17:00 ET), 99.9% otherwise
Data controls: customer-managed KMS, VPC-only egress, audit log retention 1 year
Operational: runbook for failover to private pool, on-call escalation matrix, quarterly performance reviews
throughput_requirements: burst_policy_requests: allow +50% sustained for 10 minutes; emergency burst up to 3x for 2 minutes (subject to credits)
burst_credits: 1.5M tokens/month included in committed tier; overage billed at tiered rate
reserved_gpus_plan: reserve 12 A100-equivalent GPUs (priority scheduling); flexible add-on for seasonal 4-GPU burst pool
concurrency_caps: soft cap at 120 sessions with fairness queuing; hard cap enforced post-burst window
sla_preferences: Measurement window: prefer 5-minute rolling windows for tokens/sec guarantee (legal prefers 1-min)
Remedies: service credits tiered by severity; immediate fallback to private pool for sustained underprovisioning
Monitoring: token-level telemetry, per-model latency dashboards, alert on sustained deficit >5% for 15 minutes
Change management: 30-day notice for major runtime changes; can opt into rollback of kernel changes for 90 days
